title: Redwood Docs: update streaming pages + align tool-calling examples to released SDKs
creator: Elliot Price
links: GitHub: redwood-docs#512 (update streaming guide + code tabs)
GitHub: redwood-docs#519 (tool calling docs + known pitfalls)
content:
Goal
- Refresh docs site pages for Streaming + Tool Calling so the examples are (a) consistent across languages, (b) match released SDK versions, and (c) avoid footguns called out by Support/Solutions.

Background / why
- Support keeps seeing confusion around: (1) how to assemble streaming deltas into a final message, (2) partial tool-call arguments arriving over multiple events, and (3) structured output JSON parse failures when users try to parse mid-stream.
- The docs site currently contains a mix of pre-refresh snippets (older payload shapes, different event naming) and a few newer examples, which breaks the “single mental model” goal.

In-scope pages
1) Streaming guide
- Update streaming narrative to follow the canonical event model conventions.
- Ensure code tabs for Python/TypeScript/Go implement the same loop shape:
  - handle event types explicitly
  - append text deltas to an output buffer
  - accumulate tool-call arguments across partial events
  - finalize on a single terminal event and show assembled output
- Add an “Error + retry” section with minimal guidance (don’t over-specify protocol; show what to log + when to retry).

2) Tool calling overview
- Ensure the docs reflect Redwood-supported semantics:
  - tool definitions (name/description/parameters)
  - tool call messages + tool result messages
  - parallel tool calls (multiple tool calls before responding with tool results)
- Add a “Known pitfalls” section (partial args, truncated args in logs, parallel results ordering, model-specific behavior).

3) Code sample UX
- Fix code-tab selector issues on streaming pages (internal ticket INT-3321).
- Validate copy button behavior and line wrapping for long schemas / tool parameter blocks.

SDK version alignment policy for these pages
- Docs examples must run against the latest released versions as of publish date.
- Where API surface differs by SDK version, add an explicit callout block (“If you’re on <older version>, see …”), but do NOT embed multiple diverging snippets in the main flow.
- Pin versions in snippet comments (lightweight) and in “Requirements” text (explicit):
  - Python: redwood-sdk-python >= 1.9.x
  - TypeScript: redwood-sdk-typescript >= 0.12.x
  - Go: redwood-sdk-go >= 0.8.x
(Note: exact minimums should match what Release Coordination confirms in #eng-releases; avoid implying unreleased APIs.)

Acceptance criteria (Definition of Done)
- Streaming guide code tabs use the canonical event model and do not reference deprecated event/payload fields.
- Tool calling docs show parallel tool calls + tool result loop, matching examples repo patterns.
- All snippets are copy/paste runnable with environment variables documented.
- Docs build passes, link checks pass, and code-tab selector issue is verified fixed.
- PM terminology sign-off applied (structured output vs JSON mode phrasing) and links to compatibility notes are included.

Implementation notes / decisions captured during work
- We should not suggest parsing JSON “as it streams” for structured output; streaming sections should steer users to assemble full content first, then validate.
- Add explicit note: tool-call arguments may arrive fragmented; examples must accumulate arguments before JSON.parse.
- Add compatibility link for OpenAI-compat differences instead of trying to fully explain alternative payload shapes inline.

Test plan
- Local docs build + preview.
- Manually verify each language tab:
  - code renders without wrapping artifacts
  - copy button produces runnable code (no hidden characters)
  - imports match released SDKs
- Run link checker; verify redirects don’t break existing inbound links.

Rollout plan
- Merge docs PR(s) behind the same publish window as SDK releases (coordinate with Connor O’Brien).
- Post in #announcements with links to updated streaming/tool calling pages.
- Monitor: docs page analytics + support ticket trend (SUP tickets tagged streaming/tool-calling) for 1–2 weeks.

Progress / updates
- 2025-02-07 (Wei): Drafted streaming guide rewrite; replaced older “message.delta” nomenclature with canonical event types. Added explicit accumulator pattern for tool args.
- 2025-02-10 (Elliot): Requested we keep the streaming guide focused; move structured output deep dive to the structured output page and link out.
- 2025-02-12 (Dana): Confirmed TS snippet needs to avoid the older tool result union shape; docs must match the updated TS typing work.
- 2025-02-14 (Wei): Added “Known pitfalls” bullets based on SUP-18421 + SUP-18436 themes (args fragmentation; invalid JSON; retry guidance).
- 2025-02-18 (Wei): Integrated PM terminology edits (structured output wording + model support phrasing) and added compat link.
- 2025-02-20 (Wei): Verified code-tab selector fix in preview build; confirmed copy button works on all tabs.
- 2025-02-26 (Wei): Published with docs-2025.02 release; monitored for 24h—no broken links reported.

PRs shipped
- redwood-docs#512: Update streaming guide content + align code tabs to canonical event handling
- redwood-docs#519: Refresh tool calling docs + add known pitfalls section + link to runnable samples
- redwood-docs#534: Fix broken code-tab selector regression impacting streaming pages

Follow-ups
- If we see continued confusion around partial args, add a short “debug checklist” section (what to log; how to detect incomplete JSON) rather than expanding the core example.
- After PM-413 lands, add a small structured-output support matrix callout link on the streaming page (keep it minimal; no tables inline).
